rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, and mood-doesn't-resolve-early into one verdict.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run check: the lecture never names Ronacher's three-pattern or the practitioner attributions reserved for the closing lecture what-packaging-is.md — confirmed against the module's own 'Closing lecture pre-empt' push-back guard. Module-to-module arc: the lecture correctly abstains from owning the M4→M5 or M5→M6 bridges (module file learn-from-the-test.md's 'Start here' and '## Next' sections carry those); the lecture's own close ('the whole point of packaging is that you can leave the room') hands off to the exercise without claiming sequencing authority. Big Idea fidelity: module Big Idea is 'Read the un-packaged Module 4 run through three failure-mode lenses, build the validation that would have caught each... The contrast is the lesson' (learn-from-the-test.md line 4) — the lecture leads with exactly this diagnostic-then-contrast framing and defers the build to the exercise, matching the Big Idea's own sequencing. Mood doesn't resolve early: the lecture states the stance, the lenses, and one operational primitive, but withholds the resolution itself — 'Hands-off option two' names three descriptive future artefacts without naming what they are, and 'Option two is what the exercise builds' explicitly defers the felt contrast to the exercise rather than pre-resolving it; the M5→M6 mood transition (learning through contrast → practitioner fluency) is untouched. Minor non-blocking observation: the maintainer block's own 'Watch-fors (delivery)' line 1 instructs the trainer to land '"Read first, fix later" is the load-bearing line' — but the body's actual bolded stance reads 'Diagnose first. Fix later.' (line 6), not 'Read first, fix later.' Same discipline, different verb; the strategy doc itself uses 'read first, fix later' when naming the M5 spirit (content-strategy line 381). This is a maintainer-block wording drift, invisible to students, not a body defect — worth a one-line maintainer-block sync fix so the trainer's cue quotes the line that's actually on the slide.
